A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the universal approximation theorems for neural networks can be made to hold in any dimension, for any symmetry group, for any combination of symmetries, and that the number of parameters required to do so is small, and independent of the number of input dimensions.

the universal approximation theorem for O($d$) equivariance is a consequence of the universal approximation theorem of multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) for scalar functions, with the additional insight that scalar products can be used as the basis functions for MLPs.
we show that the universal approximation theorem for O($d$) equivariant functions is equivalent to the universal approximation theorem in classical physics.
The main takeaway from our work is that

equivariant machine learning is not only about enforcing symmetries, it is also about exploiting the universal expressivity of scalars, which are the simplest and most efficient objects in physics and mathematics.
, when we want to build neural networks that are equivariant to the fundamental symmetrues and coordinate freedoms of the world, we can do so by building networks of scalars.
